newsitem.title: CANADA: Govt' said ready to impose Alcan settlement.
newsitem.headline: Govt' said ready to impose Alcan settlement.

text.p: The Canadian province of British Columbia is ready to impose a settlement on Alcan Aluminium Ltd this week over the cancellation of Alcan's Kemano hydroelectric project, the Vancouver Sun reported on Tuesday.

The two sides have failed to reach a settlement in more than two years of sporadic negotations. The province canceled construction of the half-built project in 1995 after Alcan had spent C$535 million on it.

"We've not reached an agreement, although we're very close, so we've been looking at a variety of legislative options to deal with Alcan and we are right down to the wire now," Premier Glen Clark was quoted as saying.
The company earlier this year filed a lawsuit, which it said protected its right to sue the government for compensation.
Alcan spokesman Ray Castelli dismissed Clark's comments as "sabre rattling" and "political theater."
He said negotiations on a settlement had made good progress. But if the government did introduce legislation to impose a settlement, Alcan would break off talks, he said.

"We are in very serious discussions (with the province on a settlement). We are probably closer to a resolution than we have ever been. Still there are a number of serious issues to be resolved, any one of which could be a deal breaker," he said.
Provincial government officials were not immediately available for comment.

The two sides have been working on proposals under which Alcan would receive electric power from the provincial utility, which it would use to expand its Kitimat aluminum smelter in British Columbia. The province has insisted that any deal include an expansion in employment.
The Vancouver Sun said Clark did not intend to legislate away Alcan's right to sue but could seek to make it difficult for the company to win a large financial settlement.
